questions.question: Name two unique identifiers for print documents.
questions.solution_html:
• DOI (Digital Object Identifier): A persistent alphanumeric string assigned to documents
  • providing a permanent link to their online location.
  • ISBN (International Standard Book Number): A unique identifier for books, used to distinguish
  • editions and formats.
  • ISSN (International Standard Serial Number): A unique identifier for serial publications like
  • journals, magazines, and periodicals.
  • ORCID (Open Researcher and Contributor ID): A unique identifier for authors and researchers to
  • distinguish them in academic publications.
  • PMID (PubMed Identifier): A unique identifier for articles indexed in PubMed, primarily used for
  • biomedical literature.
  • ArXiv ID: A unique identifier for preprints and papers in the ArXiv repository, commonly used in
  • physics and other sciences.
  • URN (Uniform Resource Name): A unique identifier for documents or resources in a particular
  • namespace, used to provide a persistent link over time.
  • Handle: A system of persistent identifiers used to uniquely identify digital objects, commonly
  • employed in institutional repositories. (CO 3)
  • Marking
  • a. Any 2 of the above is written Full Mark b. Any related idea Half Mark c. Any attempt
  • 2/5 Mark
questions.final_answer: DOI (Digital Object Identifier): A persistent alphanumeric string assigned to documents

questions.question: Describe how libraries have evolved from ancient times to modern times.
questions.solution_html:
• Ancient Libraries: Early libraries focused on the preservation and storage of knowledge, typically
  • housed in temples or palaces, such as the Library of Alexandria.
  • Medieval Libraries: Libraries during the middle Ages were mainly monastic, preserving religious and
  • classical texts through hand-copying manuscripts.
  • Renaissance Libraries: Marked by the rise of humanism, these libraries began to collect a wider
  • range of texts, including secular knowledge, and were often privately owned or in royal courts.
  • Public Libraries: In the 17th and 18th centuries, public libraries began to emerge, making knowledge
  • more accessible to the general public and democratizing learning.
  • Academic and Research Libraries: These libraries evolved to support scholarly research and
  • academic education, focusing on specialized collections, journals, and databases.
  • Modern Libraries: Today, libraries support various functions, including digital access to resources
  • community services, information literacy, and research collaboration.
  • Digital Libraries: With the advent of the internet and technology, libraries have transformed into
  • digital spaces, providing access to e-books, databases, and digital archives.
  • Library as a Community Hub: Libraries have increasingly become centers for social and cultural
  • activities, offering spaces for learning, collaboration, and civic engagement.
  • Specialized Libraries: Libraries serving specific industries or interests, such as law libraries, medical
  • libraries, and corporate libraries, evolved to meet the needs of specialized communities.
  • Virtual Libraries: Fully online libraries that provide resources and services without a physical space
  • catering to global access via the web. (CO 1)
  • Marking
  • a. Any 5-6 of the above is written Full Mark
  • b. Any related idea Half Mark c. Any attempt 3/10 Mark
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025
questions.final_answer: b. Any related idea Half Mark c. Any attempt 3
